findings.reason: The diff deletes the end-of-stream check, so line 241 returns state.stream unconditionally, and a document is only pushed on POP (line 232). It also deletes the `!frame` guards: line 155 reads frame.kind on a possibly undefined frame, and line 230 uses `pop()!` and then reads frame.kind. eventsToAst is publicly exported (src/index.ts:193), and constructor.ts:321/439/456 still keep the same checks.
findings.claim: The change removes all three structural checks from eventsToAst. An incomplete event stream now silently drops open documents, and a node event outside a document or an unbalanced POP now throws a bare TypeError instead of a positioned YAMLException.
findings.evidence: The diff deletes `if (state.frames.length !== 0) throwErrorAt(parserState, state.position, 'unexpected end of event stream')`, and line 241 now just does `return state.stream`. A document is only pushed to the stream on EVENT_POP (line 232). eventsToAst, createParserState, parseEvents and the event types are all public exports (src/index.ts:88-89,193), so callers can pass in event streams that are incomplete. The sibling constructor still keeps this check (src/parser/constructor.ts:456).

findings.reason: Line 223 now slices directly. NO_RANGE is -1 (line 39), so slice(-1, end) can return the input's last character instead of ''. The built-in parser always sets a range, so only hand-built events through the public API are affected, which keeps this low.
findings.claim: The alias handler dropped the NO_RANGE guard, so an AliasEvent with anchorStart -1 now depends on String.slice handling negative indices.
findings.evidence: Line 223 is now `const name = parserState.input.slice(event.anchorStart, event.anchorEnd)`. The removed code returned '' when `event.anchorStart === NO_RANGE`, and constructor.ts:426-428 still does. The parser itself always sets a range (parser.ts:545), but AliasEvent is a public type that callers can construct.

findings.reason: A grep of test/ finds none of the removed messages ('unexpected end of event stream', 'unexpected collection end', 'outside a document'), and the diff touches no tests. This is a coverage gap rather than a defect in its own right, so severity is lowered to low.
findings.claim: No test covers the removed error paths, so the suite cannot catch the weakened handling of malformed input.
findings.evidence: A grep of test/ for 'unexpected end of event stream', 'unexpected collection end' and 'outside a document' finds nothing. The diff contains no test changes, and the packet has no story.md asking for these checks to be removed.
